messages:
raj: quick heads-up — during q4_0 bring-up of the HF -> Redwood conversion for `vicuna-13b-v2` we're seeing the streaming response cut off immediately after a lone EOS token. Not the usual multi-eos duplication we've seen before, this is early termination mid-sentence in about 7% of requests. repro below.

mia: ugh. can you paste the small repro payload and the model config?

raj: sure. minimal call we use: 
```json
POST /v1/generate
{
  \"model\": \"converted/vicuna-13b-v2-q4_0\",
  \"input\": \"Write a short paragraph about the solar system.\",
  \"max_new_tokens\": 120,
  \"stream\": true,
  \"stop\": [\"\n###\"],
  \"temperature\": 0.2
}
```
Model config snippet from conversion `config.json`: 
```json
{\n  \"eos_token_id\": 2,\n  \"bos_token_id\": 1,\n  \"pad_token_id\": 0,\n  \"forced_eos_token_id\": null,\n  \"special_tokens_map\": {\"eos_token\": \"</s>\"}\n}
```
And tokenizer shows: `tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids(['</s>']) -> [2]`

sam: are you sure it's not stop seq matching `"\n###"` hitting early? that stop looks pretty specific.

raj: I checked — the cutoffs happen even when stop is omitted. payload above has stop but we repro without it too. The stream event sequence shows an `eos` event from the model followed by stream close. The generated text sometimes has an unfinished sentence before that eos.

elsa: could be a tokenization chunking artifact after quantization. q4_0 hooks sometimes merge subtokens so the model emits the `</s>` sentinel slightly earlier than the text finalization. Did you try streaming with `skip_special_tokens=false` or mapping the sentinel differently?

raj: tried `skip_special_tokens=false` on the client, same behaviour. Also tried forcing `forced_eos_token_id` to -1 in config at conversion time — didn't help.

sam: can you paste the raw streaming events (redwood runtime events) — we want to see token ids and kv-cache positions.

raj: paste of a truncated event stream (tokens shown as ids then decoded):
```
[event] token_ids: [101, 305, 78, 402, 2]
decoded: \"The solar system consists of several major planets.\"  <-- missing trailing clause
[event] model_sent_eos: token_id=2
[event] stream_close: reason=EOS_FROM_MODEL
```

elsa: ok that layout suggests the model emitted eos token id during sampling while there were still open sentence fragments. Two hypotheses: 1) the conversion script accidentally remapped internal sentinel to a lower id (e.g., 2) that collides with a subtoken boundary after quant kernel rounding, or 2) decoding_logits post-quantization inadvertently boosted eos probability. Both have been observed at low rates.

mia: can we reproduce deterministically? if it's quant-induced, the unquantized HF checkpoint should not do this. raj, do you have the same prompt hitting the HF raw model?

raj: ran the same prompt on HF upstream (non-quant) and same conversion (but without our runtime hooks) — no premature eos. So likely quantization interaction in our runtime.

sam: let's try two quick experiments: (A) re-run conversion with `eos_token_id` set to a different unused id (e.g., 50256) and remap tokenizer at load time, (B) run a debug build of the runtime that emits the logits slice for the last 8 tokens pre-softmax so we can inspect eos logit spikes.

elsa: I'll spin a canary with A first — easier. If remapping reduces the rate to ~0% then we know it's an id collision / embedding aliasing problem. If not, B should reveal whether quantized kernels produce anomalous logit bumps for eos.

infra-bot: deploy request queued: canary/vicuna-q4-eos-remap -> 3 pods (us-west) by elsa. ETA 12m.

raj: thanks — also added a short eval: 200 randomized prompts from our benchmark set to measure premature eos rate and attach to the ticket.

mia: minor ask — include the chat templates too. i noticed chat templates that append `\nAssistant:` can sometimes create tokenization boundaries that nudge eos earlier.

raj: good point. the model was onboarded with the HF chat template that ends with `\nAssistant:`, and our streaming prefixer doesn't insert a trailing space. I'll test with/without the trailing space.

elsa: if the canary shows improvement, we'll add an automatic `eos_token_id` remap during conversion for quantized artifacts and a test that runs the 200-prompt sentinel-eos check. If not, we'll escalate to kernel/quant expert.

sam: pinging @quant-team for visibility — low-rate but production-impacting.

raj: created ticket INF-2487 with logs + eval results. Will update here once canary finishes. :thumbsup:

elsa: thanks, will post canary summary in ~30m. :party:
